question: Which of the following drug causes Pseudotumour cerebri -

CHAIN: "Gentamicin" -> "ototoxicity" -> "no known link to Pseudotumour cerebri" -> 10%

analysis: Pseudotumor cerebri, or idiopathic intracranial hypertension, is a condition characterized by increased intracranial pressure without an obvious cause. Certain medications are known to be associated with this condition, and tetracycline is one of the most well-documented drugs in this regard. The mechanism is thought to involve alterations in cerebrospinal fluid dynamics. Other options such as sparfloxacin, gentamicin, and clofazimine do not have established links to pseudotumor cerebri. Sparfloxacin is more associated with QT prolongation, gentamicin with ototoxicity, and clofazimine with skin discoloration. Therefore, based on standard medical knowledge and consensus, tetracycline is the most likely drug to cause pseudotumor cerebri.
